findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:553 — requestReschedule's `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` is never awaited (no Promise.all), and now `await getCalendar(...)` inside adds a real async dynamic-import gap before `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` is even invoked, so the handler can send success and the process can be frozen (serverless) before the calendar/video delete call is ever kicked off — booking is marked rescheduled/cancelled while the external calendar event may still exist.

packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts:125 — Same detached `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` pattern wrapped in a try/catch that only covers the synchronous forEach call (not the async callbacks); adding `await getCalendar(...)` before `deleteEvent`/`deleteMeeting` delays the actual delete call past the point where the function proceeds to send the reschedule email and returns `true`, risking the calendar/video deletion never actually firing.

packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125 — Identical detached `forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` bug as vital/lib/reschedule.ts — the added `await getCalendar(...)` defers the delete call past the try/catch and past the function's return, so calendar/video cleanup can silently never happen while the reschedule reports success.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:460 — In the recurring-event branch, `apiDeletes` is populated from inside `.forEach(async (credential) => {...})` which is not awaited; the new `await getCalendar(credential)` adds an extra async (dynamic-import) gap before the inner loop even starts pushing promises into `apiDeletes`, increasing the chance that `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 runs before all recurring-event calendar deletes are even enqueued, so some external calendar deletions for recurring bookings are silently dropped while the DB rows are already cancelled.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:617 — await apiDeletes;` awaits a plain array (not `Promise.all(apiDeletes)`), a pre-existing no-op that resolves immediately regardless of pending calendar/video deletes; this is now more consequential because the recurring-branch race above (line 460) can leave `apiDeletes` under-populated or pending, meaning the paid-booking rejection path responds 200 without ever waiting on the calendar deletion promises.

goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `packages/app-store/index.ts` so each `appStore.<app>` value is now a dynamic `import(...)` (i.e., a `Promise`), whereas previously it was a resolved module namespace. The diff also shows multiple call sites updated to `await appStore[...]` (e.g. `getCalendar`, `videoClient`, payment handlers), confirming consumers must now remember to `await`. The finding’s core concern is diff-grounded: if any consumer forgets `await` and then uses the common guard pattern `if (app && "lib" in app && ...)`, the check will evaluate false on a Promise object and fall into the "not implemented" branch rather than throwing—this is a real maintainability/architecture risk created by the change, even though the diff itself updates several usages and does not show a concrete missed-`await` bug in the shown hunks.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` the diff changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) => { ... })` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...) ... })`. `Array.prototype.forEach` does not await async callbacks, so the router logic will not wait for `getCalendar()` (now async due to dynamic imports) nor for `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` to complete.
